stemMd: Who designed the dome of Florence Cathedral, Santa Maria del Fiore, built between 1420 and 1436?
explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** The dates. A dome built between 1420 and 1436 belongs to the early fifteenth century, the very start of the Renaissance in Florence. That alone rules out architects who were born later or who died long before.

**The fact that settles it.** Filippo Brunelleschi (1377-1446) directed the building of the dome from 1420 until its completion in 1436. He raised it without the full timber centring that such a span would normally need, using a double shell and bricks laid in a herringbone pattern. It is the founding work of Renaissance architecture.

**How to check it.** Test each other name against the dates. Giotto died in 1337, more than eighty years before work on the dome began. Bramante was born in 1444 and Michelangelo in 1475, both after the dome was finished. Alberti was alive at the time, but he was a theorist and designer of other buildings, not the dome's builder.

distractorRationale.a: Michelangelo is famous for a great dome - but it is the dome of St Peter's in Rome, which he designed in the sixteenth century. He was born in 1475, almost forty years after the Florence dome was completed.
distractorRationale.d: Giotto did design part of the cathedral complex: the bell tower (campanile) beside it, begun in 1334. Confusing the campanile with the dome points to him, but he died in 1337, long before the dome was started.
distractorRationale.e: Bramante is linked to the first design for the new St Peter's in Rome (1506) and to the Tempietto of San Pietro in Montorio. He was born in 1444, eight years after the Florence dome was finished.
distractorRationale.b: Alberti was a contemporary of Brunelleschi and admired his dome, which makes him a tempting pick. But Alberti's architecture lies elsewhere - the facade of Santa Maria Novella in Florence and the Tempio Malatestiano in Rimini - and he is best known for his treatise on architecture, De re aedificatoria.

accessibilityText: Question: who designed the dome of Florence Cathedral, Santa Maria del Fiore, built between 1420 and 1436? The choices are Michelangelo Buonarroti, Leon Battista Alberti, Filippo Brunelleschi, Giotto di Bondone and Donato Bramante.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank for the TIL-A History and general knowledge section. The distractors are all major Italian architects: one tied to another famous dome, one to the same cathedral's bell tower, and two Renaissance contemporaries or successors whose birth dates or known works rule them out.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Brunelleschi designed and built the dome from 1420 to 1436. Giotto designed the campanile, Alberti wrote about the dome but did not design it, and Michelangelo and Bramante came later. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: Brunelleschi designed the dome of Santa Maria del Fiore (1420-36). Giotto designed the bell tower, and Alberti, Michelangelo and Bramante are plausible but wrong names. Only C is correct.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: the dome of Santa Maria del Fiore (1420-1436) is by Brunelleschi. Giotto (died 1337) designed the campanile; Bramante (born 1444) and Michelangelo (born 1475) were born after the dome was complete; Alberti designed other buildings and was not its architect.
